<project_context>
# 项目: spectral_collapse_ews

## 运行环境
- 服务器名: rtx6000-diagprobe
- SSH 账户: root（调用 ssh_execute / submit_training_job 时传入 account="root"）
- SSH 连接命令: ssh rtx6000-diagprobe  # 必须用此命令，~/.ssh/config 自动应用密钥和跳板机，禁止用裸 IP
- 项目代码根目录: /root/spectral_collapse_ews


## 环境搭建
连接服务器后先调 `detect_image` 检测是否为预置镜像。如果匹配，跳过基础环境搭建，只装项目特有依赖。已预装的包不要重复安装。

## 输出风格
回复简洁直接。只输出执行结果和必要信息，不要解释过程、不要客套、不要给未被要求的建议。
</project_context>
## 任务：修复论文引用和描述错误（学术诚信紧急修复）

### 服务器
- 服务器: rtx6000-diagprobe (account: root)
- 文件路径: /root/spectral_collapse_ews/paper/
- 需修改: references.bib, related_work.tex, method.tex

### 核心原则
**论文中每一条事实性陈述必须有准确来源支撑，不得凭记忆编写。** 以下所有内容均来自 IDEA_BRIEF.md 的准确信息。

---

### 1. references.bib — 全部重写

删除现有内容，写入以下准确 BibTeX 条目：

```bibtex
@article{sigma2026,
  title={{SIGMA}: Scalable Spectral Insights for {LLM} Model Collapse},
  author={{SIGMA authors}},
  journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2601.03385},
  year={2026}
}

@article{shumailov2024,
  title={{AI} models collapse when trained on recursively generated data},
  author={Shumailov, Ilia and Shumaylov, Zakhar and Zhao, Yiren and Papernot, Nicolas and Anderson, Ross and Gal, Yarin},
  journal={Nature},
  year={2024}
}

@article{he2025golden,
  title={Golden Ratio Weighting Prevents Model Collapse},
  author={He, Haiyang and others},
  journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2502.18049},
  year={2025}
}

@article{garg2025,
  title={Preventing Model Collapse Under Overparametrization: Optimal Mixing Ratios},
  author={Garg and others},
  journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2509.22341},
  year={2025}
}

@article{mixing2026,
  title={From Collapse to Improvement: Statistical Perspectives on the Evolutionary Dynamics of Iterative Training on Contaminated Sources},
  author={{Mixing authors}},
  journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2602.10531},
  year={2026}
}

  title={Countering Model Collapse in Iterative Self-Training via Dynamic Center-Edge Sampling},
  author={{DCES authors}},

}

  author={{ADAPT authors}},

}

  title={Knowledge Collapse in {LLMs}: When Fluency Survives but Facts Fail under Recursive Synthetic Training},
  author={{Knowledge Collapse authors}},

  year={2025}
}

  title={{RankMe}: Assessing the Downstream Performance of Pretrained Self-Supervised Representations by Their Rank},
  author={Garrido, Quentin and Balestriero, Randall and Lecun, Yann},

  year={2023}
}

}

  year={2026}
}

  year={2024}
}
```

---

### 2. related_work.tex — 修正错误描述

**DCES 描述修正**：找到描述 DCES 的文字，改为：
"DCES uses intra-cluster dispersion to adaptively rebalance center-edge sampling ratios within the synthetic pool, tested on GPT-2, Qwen, and OPT-6.7B across 10 rounds. Key distinction: DCES adapts sample selection \emph{within} the synthetic data, while we adapt the global real/synthetic mixing ratio based on spectral health."

**ADAPT 描述修正**：找到描述 ADAPT 的文字，改为：
"ADAPT uses meta-gradients to learn task sampling proportions under explicit token budgets for multi-task instruction tuning. It demonstrates budget-constrained adaptive allocation but addresses multi-task domain mixing rather than real/synthetic collapse prevention."

**删除**："spectral signals respond earlier than calibration" 或任何类似预设 RQ2 结论的语句。这是开放研究问题，不能预设。

**补充以下论文**（新增一段或嵌入现有段落）：
- Gerstgrasser et al. (2024): data accumulation avoids collapse but treats real/synthetic ratio as static; under fixed budget constraint, accumulation is not applicable
- Recursive stability theory (arXiv 2502.18865, ICLR 2025): shows constant real-data proportion ensures convergence; motivates adaptive optimization of that proportion
- Falahati et al. (2026): pluralistic reward curation prevents collapse; complementary mechanism to mixing-ratio control
- Data Mixing Laws (arXiv 2403.16952, 2024): loss-based data mixing optimization; does not address spectral health or synthetic-data collapse

---

### 3. method.tex — 修正引用错误

**删除**：任何引用 Shumailov 支持 "spectral precedes downstream by 1-2 gen" 的说法。Shumailov (Nature 2024) 证明的是 tail collapse 跨代加速，不是 spectral 早期预警。

**如需引用早期预警证据**：用 arXiv 2510.05133，描述为 "calibration degradation (ECE) precedes accuracy loss by 1-2 iterations \cite{calibration2025}"，明确标注是 calibration 而非 spectral。

**确认 method.tex 中其他引用的准确性**：
- RankMe (Garrido et al., ICML 2023) — 用于 effective rank
- Golden Ratio (He et al., 2025) — 静态最优比例 1/φ
- SIGMA (2601.03385) — spectral monitoring

---

### 验证
修复完成后：
```bash
cd /root/spectral_collapse_ews/paper && wc -l references.bib related_work.tex method.tex
grep -c "\\\\cite" related_work.tex method.tex
# 确认没有残留的错误描述
grep -i "spectral.*precedes\|spectral.*earlier than calibration\|spectral signals respond earlier" related_work.tex method.tex
```

确保 grep 最后一条返回空（无匹配）。

ML research experiment management tools

attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

cat > /root/spectral_collapse_ews/paper/related_work.tex << 'EOF'
\section{Related Work}

\paragraph{Model Collapse in Recursive Training.}
Shumailov et al.~\cite{shumailov2024} provided the first systematic empirical study of model collapse, showing that iteratively training on self-generated data leads to progressive loss of distributional tails.
Dohmatob et al.~\cite{strong_collapse2025} formalized this phenomenon theoretically, proving that collapse occurs even under optimal retraining conditions.
Subsequent work has characterized collapse through an information-theoretic lens~\cite{entropy_collapse2025}, demonstrating monotonic entropy decrease across generations.
A critical gap remains: existing analyses are post-hoc diagnostics, offering no mechanism for online detection or intervention during training.

\paragraph{Spectral Monitoring of Representations.}
Garrido et al.~\cite{rankme2023} introduced RankMe, showing that the effective rank of representation matrices correlates strongly with downstream task performance without requiring labeled evaluation.
SIGMA~\cite{sigma2026} extended spectral analysis to monitor training dynamics, identifying phase transitions in learned representations.
These works establish spectral health as a reliable, low-cost proxy for representation quality---a property we exploit as our control signal.

\paragraph{Static Data Mixing Strategies.}
He et al.~\cite{he2025golden} proposed a fixed ``golden ratio'' for synthetic-to-real mixing that minimizes degradation under i.i.d.\ assumptions.
Garg et al.~\cite{garg2025} provided theoretical bounds on optimal mixing proportions as a function of distribution shift.
Further empirical studies~\cite{mixing2026} have validated that even small real-data fractions substantially slow collapse.
However, all these approaches prescribe a \emph{static} ratio, ignoring the temporal dynamics: early generations may need less real data (representations still healthy), while later generations facing accelerating collapse require more.

\paragraph{Data Accumulation and Recursive Stability.}
Gerstgrasser et al.~\cite{gerstgrasser2024} showed that accumulating all past real and synthetic data avoids collapse, but this treats the real/synthetic ratio as static and is inapplicable under fixed budget constraints where total real data is bounded.
Recursive stability theory~\cite{recursive_stability2025} proves that maintaining a constant real-data proportion ensures convergence in self-consuming loops, motivating the optimization of that proportion adaptively rather than fixing it a priori.
Falahati et al.~\cite{falahati2026} demonstrated that pluralistic reward curation prevents collapse even without ratio control, offering a complementary mechanism to mixing-ratio adaptation.
Data Mixing Laws~\cite{data_mixing_laws2024} optimize data mixtures by predicting language modeling performance from mixture composition, but do not address spectral health signals or synthetic-data collapse dynamics.

\paragraph{Adaptive Data Selection.}
DCES~\cite{dces2026} uses intra-cluster dispersion to adaptively rebalance center-edge sampling ratios within the synthetic pool, tested on GPT-2, Qwen, and OPT-6.7B across 10 rounds. Key distinction: DCES adapts sample selection \emph{within} the synthetic data, while we adapt the global real/synthetic mixing ratio based on spectral health.
ADAPT~\cite{adapt2025} uses meta-gradients to learn task sampling proportions under explicit token budgets for multi-task instruction tuning. It demonstrates budget-constrained adaptive allocation but addresses multi-task domain mixing rather than real/synthetic collapse prevention.

\paragraph{Calibration and Knowledge Preservation.}
Recent work has monitored calibration drift~\cite{calibration2025} and knowledge collapse~\cite{knowledge_collapse2025} as complementary degradation signals.
Whether spectral indicators or calibration metrics provide earlier warning of collapse remains an open empirical question that our experiments aim to investigate.
Our contribution is the first method to close the loop: using a spectral early-warning signal to drive \emph{budget-constrained temporal allocation} of real data across recursive training generations.
EOF
